title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π̂ = π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Its generators are the loops l_0, l_1, l_∞, with l_0 l_∞ l_1 = 1.
- ρ is the order-3 automorphism permuting the punctures cyclically: ρ(l_0) = l_1, ρ(l_1) = l_∞, ρ(l_∞) = l_0.
- σ_∞ is the involution swapping 0 and 1, so σ_∞(l_0) = l_1.
- Ĝ⁺_{0,3} = Π̂ ⋊ Z/3 is generated by Π̂ and ρ. It sits inside the S_3-extension Ĝ_{0,3}, which also contains σ_∞ and 'half-loops' ε_0 with ε_0² = l_0 and ρ^{-1}σ_∞ = ε_0^{-1}.

Where this comes from. On the previous page (Th. 327) the problem of finding the u (the 'loop equation' data) is reduced to one condition (51) on ξ = l_0^γ h_0^{-1}, with γ = (p−1)/2:
- (51) ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, equivalently (52) (ξρ)³ = 1.
- So the solutions ξ are the 1-cocycles of Z/3 acting on Π̂ via ρ, i.e. the order-3 lifts of ρ.
- Π̂ acts on them by twisted conjugation ξ ↦ λ ξ ρ(λ)^{-1} (54).
- The orbits are therefore the nonabelian cohomology set H¹(Z/3, Π̂), or equivalently the Π̂-conjugacy classes of splittings of Ĝ⁺_{0,3} → Z/3.

This page. Grothendieck assumes, 'quitte à le vérifier', that there are exactly two classes.
1. The trivial class ξ = 1. Its orbit consists of the coboundaries ξ = λ ρ(λ)^{-1} (55).
2. The class of σ_∞ ρ^{-1} σ_∞, which is another element of order 3 lying over ρ. Writing σ_∞ ρ^{-1} σ_∞ = ξ_ρ ρ, he computes, using σ_∞² = 1 and ρ^{-1}σ_∞ = ε_0^{-1}:
   ξ_ρ = σ_∞ ρ^{-1} σ_∞ ρ^{-1} = σ_∞ ε_0^{-2} σ_∞ = σ_∞(l_0^{-1}) = l_1^{-1}.
   He checks the cocycle condition: l_1^{-1} ρ(l_1^{-1}) ρ²(l_1^{-1}) = l_1^{-1} l_∞^{-1} l_0^{-1} = (l_0 l_∞ l_1)^{-1} = 1.
   He also notes that l_0^{-1} lies in the same orbit, since l_0 · l_0^{-1} · ρ(l_0)^{-1} = l_1^{-1}. Hence the second orbit is {λ l_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1}} (56).
3. He then starts case A (ξ a coboundary), where h_0 = ξ^{-1} l_0^γ = ρ(λ) λ^{-1} l_0^γ (55'). On the next page this becomes the condition σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ l_0^γ (60).

Modern reading. This is a computation of H¹(Z/3, π̂_1(P^1 − 3 pts)) in the service of solving Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations.
- The order-3 relation (51) is the hexagon relation (II) of GT in cocycle form.
- The later condition (60) is the 2-cycle relation (I) twisted by γ.
- Topologically, Π ⋊ Z/3 is the orbifold fundamental group of (P^1 − {0,1,∞})/μ_3: one puncture and two cone points of order 3, the images of the two fixed points of ρ. Hence Π ⋊ Z/3 ≅ Z/3 ∗ Z/3, and its profinite completion is a profinite free product.
- The order-3 elements over ρ are conjugate to one of the two factor generators, giving exactly two classes. One corresponds to each fixed point of ρ on P^1.
errors: The 'exactly two classes' claim is assumed, not proved. It is true: Π̂⋊Z/3 ≅ Z/3 ∐̂ Z/3 (profinite free product), and finite subgroups of a profinite free product are conjugate into a factor (Herfort–Ribes 1985). Discrete orbifold reasoning alone does not prove it profinitely.
Small notational slips only: the page writes ξ_ρ for the cocycle and uses the same letter as the solution ξ; the computations themselves check out (σ_∞²=1, ρ^{-1}σ_∞=ε_0^{-1}, ε_0²=l_0, ρ(l_0)=l_1).

ideas.what: Interpreting the order-3 (hexagon-type) relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 as a 1-cocycle condition, with solutions up to twisted conjugation forming H¹(Z/3, π̂_{0,3}), i.e. conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts of ρ in π̂⋊Z/3
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological interpretation of the GT hexagon relation (II)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, 'A cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group' (Invent. Math. 1997); Drinfeld (1990) for GT itself
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, GT-type ideas); the explicit computation is in these unpublished notes

ideas.what: Exactly two conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts of ρ: trivial (coboundaries λρ(λ)^{-1}) and that of σ_∞ρ^{-1}σ_∞, represented by the cocycle l_1^{-1} (equivalently l_0^{-1})
ideas.modern_name: Torsion in profinite free products (π̂⋊Z/3 ≅ Z/3 ∐̂ Z/3); classes match the two fixed points of the order-3 automorphism of P^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herfort–Ribes (1985) for the profinite torsion theorem; used in this GT context by Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Reducing the loop equation to case A (ξ a coboundary), then imposing the involution σ_∞ to get σ_∞(ξ)=l_1^γ ξ l_0^γ
ideas.modern_name: Combining GT relations (I) and (II); parametrising solutions f = λρ(λ)^{-1}

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly treats the hexagon-type relation for the loop equation as a Z/3 nonabelian-cohomology problem in π̂_{0,3}. He identifies the two orbits explicitly, with representatives 1 and l_1^{-1} ~ l_0^{-1}. This anticipates the cohomological interpretation of GT usually credited to Lochak–Schneps (1997), years before Drinfeld's GT (1990).
missed.quote: Admettons (quitte à le vérifier par la suite) qu'il y a exactement deux classes de conjugaison : celle de ξ=1 ... et d'autre part la classe de conjugaison de la relat.^n d'ordre 3 σ_∞ρ^{-1}σ_∞^{-1}=σ_∞ρ^{-1}σ_∞ de ρ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents priority and the independent genesis of the cocycle approach to GT relations inside Grothendieck's unpublished 'équation des lacets'. The non-trivial second class (cocycle l_0^{-1}) also hints at a variant family of solutions. The page sets that class aside, so its role in GT-like theories is not developed here.

missed.claim: Only case A (trivial class) is pursued on this page. The second class ξ = λ l_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1} (56) is set up but not analysed here; whether it yields further solutions of the loop equation is left open on this page.
missed.quote: A) Cas où ξ est de la forme (55), donc h_0 = ρ(λ)λ^{-1}l_0^γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Analysing the second torsion class could clarify whether the 'twisted' solutions are empty or form a separate torsor, a question on the structure of GT-type equations.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clear, explicit pre-Drinfeld computation of H¹(Z/3, π̂_{0,3}) as the key step in solving the hexagon-type loop equation, anticipating Lochak–Schneps. Specialists know Grothendieck had GT-like ideas, but this level of detail is unpublished. The mathematics itself is now known.
transcription_corrections: The letter written as ζ throughout this page is very likely the same ξ as on the previous page (eqs. 50–54).
In (55') the exponent is γ, not σ: h_0 = ρ(λ)λ^{-1}l_0^γ.
Π̂_{0,3} should be π̂_{0,3} to match the previous page's notation (the next page also uses Π̂).
In 'correspondant aux solutions tautologiques' the word is possibly 'scindages' (aux scindages tautologiques).
